statement: External renderability, external executability and native-handoff eligibility are independent constitutional properties. A capability may be unreachable externally (externalRenderAllowed: false, externalExecuteAllowed: false) and still legitimately offered to an external experience via a native handoff (nativeHandoffAllowed: true). These three properties must be represented independently in every capability descriptor, and validation must check them independently.
classification: A THREE-PROPERTY MODEL for capability residency and accessibility, replacing a conflated binary. The discovery came from the pilot's incorrect assumption that NATIVE_ONLY (render:false, execute:false) meant 'not handoff-eligible'. In fact, native handoff is the legitimate mechanism to expose a capability with those restrictions to an external consumer without violating residency constraints.

canaries.assertion: Check 6 ('surface must be either externalRenderAllowed OR a permitted nativeHandoff') and Check 7 (same for actions) must both pass for NATIVE_ONLY capabilities (render:false, execute:false) when nativeHandoffAllowed:true and handoffOffered:true. A surface with all three properties false must be rejected. Checks must apply ONLY to external-provider output (projection.provider !== 'native'); native provider output must never be rejected by disposition checks to preserve SPEC-AEE-001 §16 fail-closed guarantee.

occurrences.site: types/adaptiveExperience.ts — AdaptiveCapabilityDisposition type; services/adaptive/projectionValidator.ts — checks 6-7; services/adaptive/journeySpineAdapter.ts — buildCapabilityRefsFromJourney
occurrences.defect: Original pilot used binary NATIVE_ONLY flag which was interpreted as 'render nowhere but native', conflating three independent decisions. This led to handoff-ineligibility being assumed for NATIVE_ONLY capabilities, which is incorrect because native handoff is precisely the mechanism to expose such capabilities without violating residency.

notes: This is the foundational corrective to the pilot's architecture. All other disposition-related findings flow from this one independent property model.

The SCOPE is deliberately RECORDED AS LOCAL, not cross-architecture. Generality is earned by recurrence; one documented occurrence is not enough to claim this applies universally. Widen the scope when a second, genuinely different system/capability documents an occurrence.
The scope 'local' does NOT diminish the importance. This is a core part of AEE's architecture going forward; the local scope reflects evidentiary rigor, not significance.
